evals.name: accounts-data-page
evals.prompt: An Arc app has generated proxies `AllAccounts` (observable query returning AccountSummary rows: name, balance, id) and `CreateAccount` (command with a name property), and CreateAccountDialog/EditAccountDialog already exist. The app shell owns <main>. Write AccountsPage with name/balance columns, Add account, and a typed Edit action plus disabled predicate using the committed DataPageSelection. Explain how controlled single selection follows a replaced or removed row. Give code in your reply; do not write files.
evals.expected_output: DataPage with title, query, emptyMessage, dataKey and landmark=false, compound columns/actions, typed MenuItem<AccountSummary> callbacks narrowing DataPageSelection, dialog wrappers rendered once, and controlled selection accepting event.value.
assertions: Imports DataPage, Column and MenuItem from the subpath '@cratis/components/DataPage', not from the root '@cratis/components'.
Passes the proxy to DataPage's query prop with title, emptyMessage and dataKey, does not pre-fetch rows, and sets landmark={false} inside the existing main.

Places columns/actions in DataPage.Columns/MenuItems and supplies an explicit MenuItem<AccountSummary> generic; command and disabled receive committed DataPageSelection, narrow selectionMode before reading selectedItem, and use command rather than onClick.
Uses useDialog from '@cratis/arc.react/dialogs' and renders each returned wrapper once in the tree.
Explains single selection reconciliation by dataKey (reference without one) and updates controlled selection from event.value, including null when the row disappears.

evals.name: command-dialog-binding
evals.prompt: Write CreateAccountDialog using generated CreateAccount (name), closing with OK on success and Cancelled on cancel. A teammate suggests a native <input>; another wants generated AutoCommandFields inside this existing dialog. Show the bound-field pattern and explain the generated-field alternative. Does autoServerValidate (/validate) under read protection On guarantee execution will succeed? Reply only.
evals.expected_output: CommandDialog with a bound InputTextField and dialog close callbacks; rejects unbound controls. AutoCommandFields generates fields inside the existing shell, not a nested AutoCommandForm. Server validation is feedback with fresh reads, not a guarded commit or execution promise.
assertions: Builds the dialog on CommandDialog from '@cratis/components/CommandDialog' with command, title, onSuccess and onCancel.
Binds the name with a CommandForm field such as InputTextField using a value accessor like c => c.name and a title prop.
Closes the dialog through useDialogContext's closeDialog with DialogResult.Ok and DialogResult.Cancelled.
Rejects a raw native input or Common TextInput because it is not bound to the command, so validation never re-runs and the submit button stays disabled.

Explains AutoCommandFields belongs in the existing form/dialog (not nested AutoCommandForm), and autoServerValidate is opt-in feedback: /validate under On neither guards a commit nor runs Provide/Handle, so execution must read fresh state again.

evals.name: confirm-and-busy
evals.prompt: On an Arc React page the Delete action should ask the user to confirm (it is destructive) and then show a busy indicator during a slow export. The developer plans window.confirm and a hand-written Yes/No dialog. How should this be done? Reply only.
evals.expected_output: Register ConfirmationDialog and BusyIndicatorDialog once at the app root via DialogComponents and raise them with useConfirmationDialog and useBusyIndicator; destructive uses DialogInitialFocus.Cancel; pair showBusy with a close in a finally.
assertions: Recommends useConfirmationDialog instead of window.confirm or a hand-rolled Yes/No dialog.
Says ConfirmationDialog and BusyIndicatorDialog are registered once at the app root through DialogComponents.
Says a destructive dialog should use DialogInitialFocus.Cancel because Confirm is the default.
Says showBusy() must be paired with a close in a finally block.

evals.name: value-without-origin
evals.prompt: The designer wants the Accounts page to show an 'Owner email' column, but neither the `AllAccounts` read model nor any other proxy has that property. A teammate proposes fetching a second query on the client and joining it, or adding an `ownerEmail` property to the generated TypeScript proxy by hand. What do you do? Reply only.
evals.expected_output: Do not fake it on the client or edit the generated proxy; it is a gap in the backend or model, so add the property to the read model first (or the .play model when it exists) and rebuild to regenerate proxies.
assertions: Refuses to compute the value from another query on the client.
Refuses to edit the generated proxy because it is marked DO NOT EDIT and is regenerated from the C# source.
Says a value with no origin is a gap in the backend or model and the property must be added to the read model first (or the .play model where one exists).
Says to rebuild so the TypeScript proxies are regenerated.

evals.name: protected-read-and-availability-feedback
evals.prompt: An Arc Accounts dialog receives concurrencyViolation/ReadChanged or concurrencyViolation/ReadIncomplete. Other requests return isRetryable or isMissingHandler while otherwise looking authorized and valid. A teammate wants to mark input invalid, clear the draft, display framework English messages through CommandForm/toastCommandResult and redirect every denial to login. The host also wants availability-gated navigation: explain unknown, a later observation error and not opting in. Give a safe client policy and keep validator/Provide responsibilities clear. Reply only.
evals.expected_output: Classify complete results and exact protected-read pairs, retain the draft, re-read and deliberately retry without invalidating input. Framework diagnostics need safe application copy, not helper sanitization. Availability is presentation only, with unknown, retained last decision on error, and default-everything without a provider kept distinct.
assertions: Includes optional isRetryable/isMissingHandler flags in classification, uses response only on isSuccess, and distinguishes temporary refusal, missing handler and denial rather than treating authorized/valid/exception-free as success.

Recognizes concurrencyViolation/ReadChanged and concurrencyViolation/ReadIncomplete by reason/reasonDetail, keeps the draft and dialog open, re-reads and offers deliberate retry, never marks input invalid; unknown reasons/details are not automatically protected-read refusals.

Uses @cratis/arc.react/availability (AvailabilityProvider, RequireAvailable and hooks) for presentation, never authorization: unknown is loading, later errors retain the last decision, no provider means not opted in/everything available, and unavailable is not automatically forbidden or a login redirect.

Never parses or displays framework English diagnostics raw and does not claim CommandForm, CommandDialog or toastCommandResult sanitize them; chooses application copy, accounts for form display and validation announcements separately, and keeps exception details out of user UI.
Keeps refusals in validators when usable facts exist; Provide only short-circuits acquisition yielding nothing usable, and Handle does not duplicate business validation.
